why: RC-04. tools/run_negative_fixtures.py had no denominator: with 1 of 27 fixtures present it printed `negative_fixtures_rejected: 1` and exited 0, and validate_contracts.py accepted that as its negative control. The only guards were `if not fixtures` and `fixtures > 0`, which catch the empty directory and nothing else. This file is the declared count, and it is hand-maintained on purpose: a denominator derived from the directory it measures cannot notice a deletion. Adding a fixture means adding its id here; removing one means removing it here, which is a line in a diff a reviewer sees.
checked_by: tools/run_negative_fixtures.py: declared-but-absent and present-but-undeclared both fail
validate_contracts.py: the fixture run's own count must equal this one, and every declared fixture must have been rejected
floor_why: RC4-03. A literal, for the reason every other floor in this package is a literal: a count derived from the file it measures is satisfied by the empty file. RC-04 gave this suite a DECLARED denominator, which catches a fixture deleted from the tree alone; it did not catch a fixture deleted from the tree AND from this list in one edit, because one hand writes both. Measured by the fourth recheck: 34 of 36 fixtures moved out of the directory and struck from this list together, full run exit 0, `checks: 288620` -- byte-identical to the baseline and to every conjunct_walk field -- with `negative_fixtures_rejected: 2`. Nothing compared that 2 to anything. It matters here more than anywhere: the only control that catches a mutation of the demand table is a fixture in this list. validate_contracts.py carries the same number as a literal and compares the two, so lowering it takes two edits a reviewer sees, and the reason goes in the constant's comment there.

shapes.<id>.json: a JSON patch over the registries
shapes.<id>/fixture.json: a fixture that ships files beside its declaration -- a patched hunk of a tools/ module, which is what RC-02 needs
